hints: Notice that X must form an acidic solution with water, so think about which Period 3 oxides are acidic rather than basic or amphoteric.
Calculate the moles of NaOH used from $0.0250 \times 0.100$, then work out how many moles of $\text{SO}_3$ are in 0.100 g and how much NaOH that would need.
Remember that $\text{SO}_3$ gives diprotic $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ needing 2 NaOH, while $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ gives 4 triprotic acids, so compare the predicted titre for each.
walkthrough:
**Sort by acid-base character**

Think about Period 3 oxides first. MgO is basic, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric, while $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ and $\text{SO}_3$ are acidic.

Since X gives an acidic solution, only the non-metal oxides are possible.

**Find moles of NaOH used**

Use moles = concentration x volume in $\text{dm}^3$.

$$n(\text{NaOH}) = 0.100 \times \frac{25.0}{1000} = 0.00250 \text{ mol}$$

**Test $\text{SO}_3$**

The reactions are:
$$\text{SO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$$
$$\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 + 2\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
So 1 mol $\text{SO}_3$ needs 2 mol NaOH.

$$M_r(\text{SO}_3) = 32.1 + (3 \times 16.0) = 80.1$$
$$n(\text{SO}_3) = \frac{0.100}{80.1} = 0.00125 \text{ mol}$$
Predicted $n(\text{NaOH}) = 2 \times 0.00125 = 0.00250 \text{ mol}$. This matches exactly.

**Check $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ fails**

The reaction is:
$$\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 4\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$$
Each $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ needs 3 NaOH for full neutralisation, so 1 mol $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ needs 12 mol NaOH.

$$n(\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}) = \frac{0.100}{284.0} = 0.000352 \text{ mol}$$
This would need about $0.00422$ mol NaOH, much larger than $0.00250$ mol. So only $\text{SO}_3$ fits.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric and is insoluble in water, so it does not give an acidic solution. It would not be neutralised in this way.
options.B: Incorrect. MgO is a basic oxide. With water it gives slightly alkaline $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$, not an acidic solution, so it cannot be X.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ does give acidic $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$, but the mole ratio is wrong. 0.100 g is about 0.000352 mol and would need about 0.00422 mol NaOH for full neutralisation, almost double the 0.00250 mol actually used.
options.D: Correct. $\text{SO}_3$ is an acidic Period 3 oxide forming diprotic $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. 0.100 g is 0.00125 mol, needing $2 \times 0.00125 = 0.00250$ mol NaOH, exactly the titre observed.
